answer: Recursive Cryptographic State Forge Agents must derive their execution state from an immutable public island that shifts every block. When an agent duplicates, both instances process identical transactions from the same parent state. A background network protocol called zephyr sweeps these duplicate branches and forces them to collide in memory. The protocol detects identical output hashes at identical index slots and proofs the duplication publicly. The attacker loses all computational gas credits allocated to the clashing instances instantly.
